[roadway], j. villanueva observed the collision occur between u1 and u2. upon hearing the above-described statement, i determined that u2 could/would not have [roadway] if/since j. villanueva reportedly had a green light to turn west-to-southbound. i spoke with u2 (who appeared to behave suspiciously/uncooperatively.) u2 did not want to receive a [case id] slip. he also (initially) did not want to provide me his identifying information either. i also observed u2's eyes to appear dilated but ems staff on scene advised this was reportedly due to u2's medication that he is reportedly prescribed. i did observe there appeared to be multiple apparent injuries (which u2 described as ""road rash"") in the areas including the ""back"" portion of u2's right shoulder area, and u2's right arm area. due to witnesses advising that u1 had a red light, (therefore no right-of-way) and due to u2 reportedly not having right-of-way (due to u1 advising the light reportedly turned green just before u1 entered the intersection, and due to j. villanueva advising he reportedly had a green light to turn left as he observed u2 pass his own vehicle) i could not confidently determine which (if not both) violation(s) occurred during this incident which caused (or otherwise influenced) the collision to occur. witnesses:[roadway]., corpus christi, tx, 78414c: (361) 699-1246danny alvaradoc: (806) 632-1106mary medinac: (806) 474-9175bwc/dvr utilized.

records.deidentified_narrative: on [date] at approximately 2128 hours, i, ofc. fisher #[roadway] for a report of a subject who was run over by a vehicle. on scene, i observed a hispanic male laying [roadway]. the male was bleeding from a ~2-3"" vertical laceration the back of his head. he also had bleeding abrasions on his arms and back. he was identified as jose acetuno hernandez and his friend, wilmer barrera, was standing near him. jose was transported to [medical facility]. wilmer and witnesses said that the fleeing vehicle was a black sedan which [roadway]. wilmer did not give a better description of the fleeing vehicle but said that he argued with someone about an ""antenna"" and that jose was driving the car. adjacent to jose was a black mazda sedan txlp [identifier] (registered in his name) parked on the north curb in front of [roadway]. the mazda had heavy front passenger side collision damage that appeared new. its front passenger side tire was shredded and its wheel had deep scratches in it. it also had minor white sideswipe marks that appeared to be recent paint transfer on its passenger side rear door. its trunk was hanging open with apparently recent hand marks on it. both front airbags were deployed. there were not liquid trails from the vehicle or signs of it striking anything nearby. ofc. kavanagh explained that a witness reported that another black sedan may have been chasing the mazda. both vehicles pulled over and two subjects from each car exited and argued with each other. the second black car then backed up and drove forward, striking jose. when wilmer was asked about this, he denied speaking to anyone in a different car and omitted any mention of arguing about an ""antenna"". at the time of this report, hospital staff reported that jose had fractures to his left leg and left side ribs. noizf 9165

records.deidentified_narrative: the private parking lot at 302 s oregon is a parking lot with parking stalls on the west, and south end with an island of parking stalls on the east end. on the listed date, unit 1 stated he was completing putting a vehicle onto the bed when he got back into his vehicle. unit 1 [roadway] off when he heard his supervisor, who was on scene, honk his horn. the driver of unit 1 stated he stopped and looked at his supervisor who was pointing to the front of his tow truck. the driver of unit 1 exited his vehicle and found a pedestrian in a motorized wheelchair in front of his truck. the driver of unit 1 deduced that he had struck the pedestrian. the driver of unit 1 stated that due to the height of his truck, he didn't see the pedestrian in front of his truck. officers spoke with the pedestrian, unit 2 about what had occurred on the listed date. unit 2 stated she was coming up to the parking lot when she saw her provider's vehicle on the back of unit 1. she stated that she felt that the tow truck was too close to her, and she tried to go around it. unit 2 stated that as she tried to go around it, unit 1 pulled forward and struck her. unit 2 stated she was pushed and dragged by unit 1. unit 2 stated she banged on the truck to get unit 1 to stop. officers asked unit 2 for clarification on what had occurred and unit 2 stated again that she was trying to go around unit 1, but was struck while trying to go around it. officers observed video footage from unit 1's supervisor who captured the incident on a dashcam. in the video, unit 2 can be seen pulling up to the right side of the tow truck, stops, and then goes back around toward the front of the truck. unit 2 begins to go toward the front of the tow truck when unit 1 begins to pull forward. it appears that unit 1 begins to move first, following by unit 1 going toward the front of unit 1. unit 1 ultimately strikes unit 2. officers observed a surveillance video that shows sufficient space to the right of the tow truck where unit 2 could've waited for unit 1 to pull off to go around unit 1. unit 2 advised the officer that following the collision, she felt pain to her neck, back and left shoulder. unit 2 declined transport by fms. officers did not locate any witnesses aside from the dashcam and surveillance video. officers did not issue any citations in the collision due to it occurring on private property.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit #1 was traveling in a northern direction in the private parking lot of heb, located at [roadway], lumberton, texas 77657, and was near the front entrance doors of the grocery store. unit #1 stopped and was preparing to back into a parking space in the center of the parking lot (approx 25 feet east from the front entrance doors). as unit #1 backed up, traveling in a southern direction and into the painted yellow lines of a handicap parking space, the driver of unit #1 turned the wheel and began backing in a easterly direction outside the boundries of the handicap parking space. the driver of unit #1 continued backing slowly while approaching the driver side of unit #2 which was parked facing north in the parking lot. unit #1 then quickly acellerated and crashed into unit #2. the back left portion of unit #1 struck the left passenger side of unit #2 and the impact caused the rear end of unit #2 to move approximately six or seven feet outside the boundries of the parking space. two pedestrians, identified as unit #3 and unit #4 were standing on the back right passinger side of unit #2 during the time of the crash and were struck by unit #2. this unsafe backing incident appeared to be the result of the driver of unit #1 accidently pressing the accelerator pedal instead of the break when he intended to stop the vehicles reverse movement. note: the owner of unit #2, jake gibbins was outside of his parked prior to this crash. when gibbins witnessed unit #1 backing closer to his location, he quickly entered his vehicle through the front driver side door and avoided injury. a private property incident report was completed by the investigating officer in addition to this crash report. for further information, lumberton police department incident report # 20240508 can be reviewed. witness #1 : sgt y. borrero, beaumont police dept. began to back up and observed the top of u2's head through his back window. u1 advised he did not know that he backed into her. u1 advised that u2 was on her phone and never got off of her phone or made him aware that she was struck. u1 advised that u2 walked away and so he drove off. u2's father is the one who called to report the accident a day later from an urgent care center on another side of town. i spoke to u2 who advised she was walking through the parking lot towards her vehicle. u2 advised that she observed u1 to be parked. she received a phone call and answered the call. u2 advised that she was walking behind u1, when he placed his pickup truck in reverse and struck her. u1 advised that she said something along the lines of ""ouch"" and walked to u1's front driver side window, attempting to look inside. u2 advised that u1 did not roll down his window, but u2 did not know if he looked at her or not. u2 advised u1 drove away. i asked her if she was injured the day before in what she calls a hit and run, why she didn't notify police or ems for her injuries. u2 advised that she did not feel that she was hurt until before she was about to go to bed. u2 described her injury as being the inside part of her elbow. i am unsure at what angle u2 was struck that would cause an injury to the inside of her elbow. i did not observe any visible injuries on u2 and u2 advised that she was told there were no broken bones. u2 advised she did need an mri. there was no damage to u1's vehicle. u2's father wanted to make me aware that a u1 admitted to the supervisors at his job that he did back into u2. u1 did not deny backing into u2, he just said he was not sure because he did not feel anything, she continued to remain on the phone, he did not observe her flagging him down. i do believe that u1 thought that u2 was fine and that is why he left. u2 kept speaking to someone on the phone and u1 did not observe her attempting to speak to him. . u2 left the scene without notifying police or ems.

records.public_safe_text: while working in west patrol i was assigned for a major accident involving a pedestrian and vehicle. upon my arrival to the listed location, i observed v1 seating at a nearby bus stop being attended by medic #33. the listed vehicle had fled the scene prior to my arrival. pedestrian stated that he was walking south bound suing the crosswalk. pedestrian stated he was talking to his wife and was not really paying attention to the flow of traffic. pedestrian stated that he was suddenly hit by a red pickup (unit#1) from behind. pedestrian stated that the unit#1 continued traveling [roadway] 90. pedestrian was not able to provide details of the vehicle due to it was dark and he was hit from behind. i observed pedestrian to have a swollen left ankle with redness, both of his elbows had bloody scrapes, and the right forearm had a slight redness. w1 stated that she was seating at the [roadway] 90 on the west bound lanes. w1 stated that she observed unit#1 traveling [roadway] 90 and the traffic control light was green for the vehicle. w1 stated that she observed pedestrian walking on the crosswalk when it was not safe to do so. w1 stated that she observed when the unit#1 hit the pedestrian and continued to travel east bound. w1 stated that she observed the unit#1 return to the scene for an unknown reason but then fled again towards [roadway] 90. i contacted det myers #1366 to notify him of the incident. det. myers provided information on how to handle the call. i notified sgt. buso #3263 of the accident. det. andrade #2172 took photos [medical facility]. v1 was transported by medic #[medical facility] to be further evaluated. dme is available.
